name: synthetic_trailing_arm_axle
description: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE -- NOT AN ENGINEERING MODEL. A left/right trailing-arm single axle whose connection graph is deliberately unlike the built-in double wishbone: each side has ONE arm pivoting on a chassis revolute about the vehicle Y axis, with the wheel carried at the arm's outboard end. There are no upper/lower arms and no ball joints, so the constraint graph is a different graph and not a renamed one. Geometry, masses and units are chosen to be solvable and legible, not to represent a real vehicle. Decision D2 authorises synthetic fixtures for architecture and solve-path verification only; no engineering accuracy is claimed.

expected._note: Independently derived facts the tests assert against. They are properties of the fixture's own geometry, not measurements of a solve.
expected.dof_derivation: Each side is one free body (the arm) held to the fixed chassis by a single revolute joint. A revolute removes five of a free body's six degrees of freedom, so that side keeps exactly one: rotation about the pivot's Y axis. The wheel centre is a point rigidly attached to the arm, so its height is a function of that one rotation. This is a different *graph* from the built-in double wishbone: there the upright is held by two ball joints (the two inboard arm mounts) plus a tie rod, and the arms are separate bodies, so the constraint count and the connectivity both differ -- two revolute rows here versus thirteen rows there, and no path from any body to a rack.
expected.wheel_centre_rise_derivation: The wheel centre sits at a local offset of (dx, dy, dz) = (350, -200, 50) mm from the arm pivot, and the only joint is a revolute about the chassis Y axis. Rotating that body by theta about Y maps the offset to x' = dx*cos(theta) + dz*sin(theta), z' = -dx*sin(theta) + dz*cos(theta), so dz/dtheta at theta = 0 is -dx = -350 mm per radian. A 10 mm wheel-centre travel therefore needs theta = asin(10/350) = 0.0286 rad = 1.6372 deg. The arm is not a rigid vertical link, so this is a derived slope and not a linear spring rate; the tests assert the solved geometry against it.
expected.constraint_count_derivation: Two revolute joints, one per side. No rack joint: the fixture declares no rack body, and the case names no rack coordinate.
expected.wheel_centre_unit_direction: dz/dtheta is *negative*: rotating the arm about +Y by a positive angle moves the wheel centre downward, because the wheel centre lies forward of the pivot in +X and a positive Y rotation carries +X toward -Z.
